title: introduce-oncall-fatigue-index-and-automated-rotation-suggester
author: Evelyn Shaw
body:
Motivation: Repeatedly during incident retros and oncall interviews we see the same root causes related to responder fatigue: short recovery windows between high-alert periods, uneven distribution of noisy alerts across rotations, and opaque health signals for oncallers. This PR introduces an opt-in "On-call Fatigue Index" (OFI) and an automated rotation-suggester service that proposes gentle rota adjustments to reduce fatigue spikes.

What this change includes (high level):
- core/ofa: a small library that computes a normalized fatigue score per person per rolling window using three signals: alert_density (alerts/hour adjusted by severity), disruption_penalty (non-working-hours/overnight page factor), and recovery_deficit (minutes since last high-severity mitigation). Model is configurable via tuning constants and feature-flagged.
- cli/rotas_suggester: a command-line tool and lightweight HTTP endpoint that reads rotation configs and historical oncall telemetry and emits suggested shifts with confidence scores and expected reduction in peak OFI. Suggestions are conservative by default (minimize churn).
- dashboards/fatigue_dashboard.json: an initial Grafana dashboard (panel templates + example queries) to visualize per-rotation OFI heatmaps, rolling exposures, and top contributors.
- incident-bot integration hooks: optional webhook that surfaces high OFI alerts into incident-bot channels with recommended recovery windows and a "suggest rota" quick action.
- simulation harness: tests/simulate_rotas.py and e2e fixtures to validate that the suggester reduces peak scores in attacker scenarios.

Checklist: 
- [x] unit tests for core scoring functions (tests/test_fatigue_index.py)
- [x] integration test for suggester endpoint (tests/integration/test_rotas_suggester.py)
- [x] dashboard JSON + examples
- [x] docs: docs/oncall-fatigue.md describing the algorithm, tuning knobs, and opt-in migration path
- [x] feature flag gating + migration notes in RELEASE_NOTES.md

Backward compatibility and privacy: OFI computation does not require PII; it accepts stable user IDs and only aggregates scores. Collection is opt-in at org level; default is off. Suggester emits only rotation adjustments (no raw alert payloads) and honors redaction settings.

Performance and safety: The scoring library is intentionally lightweight (O(n) over recent alerts) and the suggester uses a constrained local-search optimizer to avoid large rota churn. We include a safe mode where suggestions must be explicitly approved by rotation owners.

- c1a3d5f: add core fatigue index and unit tests

- src/slo_toolkit/fatigue_index.py
- src/slo_toolkit/rotas_suggester.py

- dashboards/fatigue_dashboard.json

CI summary: 
- unit-tests: passed on first run
- lint: passed (black/ruff)
- integration-tests: passed after adding a timing tolerance to the simulated alert generator
- e2e: flaky in initial run (timing-related), reran and passed on second run

Review conversation (high level): 
- Marco Li: "Sketch looks good. Two asks: 1) ensure we never surface that raw alert bodies through the webhook; 2) make the default suggestion budget conservative (no more than 1 shift swap per week unless owner approves)."
- Author (Evelyn): "Addressed: webhook sends only user IDs + suggestion metadata, not alert payloads. Added `suggestion_budget` config with default=1 per-rotation/week. See commit e1f2a8b."
- Samira Khan: "Can we expose an aggregate daily OFI per-schedule so SRE managers can see long-term trends?"
- Author: "Added a daily_rollup endpoint and dashboard panel; docs updated with examples. See dashboards/fatigue_dashboard.json and src/slo_toolkit/rollups.py."
- Jonas Weber: "Unit tests look comprehensive; please add one more integration case for daylight-savings/shift boundary disruptions."
- Author: "Added DST test case to integration harness (tests/integration/test_rotas_suggester.py)."

Merge details: merged by Marco Li via squash, commit message summarizes feature and migration steps.

Operational notes: Opt-in flag `slo_toolkit.oncall_fatigue.enabled` defaults to false. Suggested rollout path: enable in a single team, validate dashboard and suggestions for 2 weeks, then expand org-wide. Emergency disable: flip feature flag and delete webhook subscription.

Related work and context: This complements previous work on shift-imbalance-detector (ENG-1793) and the "oncall-primer" efforts; it focuses on proactive mitigation rather than signal detection.

release_notes: Add optional On-call Fatigue Index (OFI) and rotation suggester. Opt-in by feature flag. Provides per-rotation fatigue scoring, dashboard panels, and safe suggestions to reduce peak responder fatigue. Backwards compatible and privacy-preserving.
